meta.title: Cloudnine — launch, 14 January 2027
meta.description: Launch deck for Cloudnine, a ten-minute evening wind-down app: the problem, the reveal, three features one per slide, beta proof, a clinician's voice, pricing and launch date.

slides.heading: Fall asleep in 21 minutes, not 38.
slides.lead: A ten-minute wind-down for your evening, on iOS and Android.
slides.notes: Read the headline slowly. Both numbers come from our beta; we prove them on slide 8.

slides.quote: I'm in bed at eleven and still scrolling at one. Then the alarm goes at six.

slides.heading: One button starts your evening and shows how you slept
slides.lead: Tap Begin at bedtime. Wake to last night's number.

slides.heading: How it works
slides.lead: Dim, breathe, drift. Ten minutes in all.

Notifications wait until 07:00.

slides.heading: A drifting cloud paces four minutes of 4-7-8 breathing
slides.lead: Follow the cloud. No counting, no screen glare.
slides.imageAlt: A breathing wave with a cloud marking the hold phase: in 4 seconds, hold 7, out 8

slides.body:
The story stops when you stop moving.
240 stories at launch.

slides.heading: Testers fell asleep 17 minutes sooner within six weeks
slides.lead: n = 12,400 beta testers · phone-sensor sleep onset · Sep–Oct 2026
slides.notes: The drop is steepest in week one. Say that most people feel it by the third night.

slides.heading: Four in five testers still open it nightly after six weeks
slides.label: nightly use in week 6

slides.quote: We now hand Cloudnine to every new parent who leaves our clinic.
slides.by: Dr Ana Ferreira, head of sleep medicine, Lumen Health

slides.heading: Free to start, $4.99 a month for every story
Tonight, fall asleep in 21 minutes
slides.lead: Pre-order now: your first month of Plus is free.
slides.notes: End on the cover promise. Point at the date, then stop talking.
